object: FIELD INDEX / AXIAL LATEST unified focus compositor

before.root: LATEST chronology, compact attention marks, issues and map existed as separate readings.
before.interaction: Row/map selection generally navigated or maintained separate local selections; the simplified root was mid-transition and still carried legacy strip assumptions.
before.axial: AXIAL 0.6.1 existed as a separate PROOF_REQUIRED Foundry instrument over FIELD/HOUSE.

operation: Graft AXIAL 0.6.1 STRIP mechanics into the root LATEST reading.
Derive four unequal vocabularies from live manifest data: ROUTE, STATE, OPERATION and WORK MODE.
Use one fixed bright focus gate across all four strips.
Make ROUTE selection align the other axes back to the exact source identity.
Make STATE/OPERATION/WORK MODE selection filter real manifest routes; no exact intersection returns an explicit no-match state.
Share one focus identity across AXIAL strips, plain newest-first rows, HEADS/ports selectors and MAP projections.
Separate selection from navigation: clicking selects; OPEN is explicit.
Keep the ordinary chronological list directly below AXIAL as the plain source reading.

after.external_projection: selected route → Scale Lens via scale.lens.handoff.v01
after.authority: CURRENT owns attention; AXIAL selection does not mutate manifest/current state.

verification.sample_tuple_check: Newest 12 manifest routes each had a unique STATE × OPERATION × first WORK MODE tuple at validation time.

residue: No comparative usability evidence yet; the embedded AXIAL compositor is an operational experiment, not proof that it beats the plain list.
The plain chronological list remains authoritative for re-entry ordering.
AXIAL 0.6.1 remains PROOF_REQUIRED and no physical-cylinder claim transfers into FIELD INDEX.
next: Use FIELD INDEX normally. Compare whether AXIAL reduces reorientation when looking for a recent route by state/operation/work-mode; preserve the plain list as control.
